English: Wooden Palisade
A basic timber palisade, hastily erected by the faithful to mark and protect holy ground. Simple but effective against roaming bandits and wild beasts.
Stone Perimeter
A low wall of shaped stones, offering greater security and a sense of permanence to the temple precincts. The faithful feel safer within its bounds.
Defended Gatehouse
A sturdy gatehouse with reinforced doors and a place for guards or monks to watch over all who enter the holy grounds.
Watchtower Addition
The addition of watchtowers along the walls allows for early warning against threats and a symbol of vigilant faith.
Reinforced Walls
Thicker stone walls with improved foundations and defensive platforms, proof against even determined raiders.
Battlemented Parapet
High stone parapets with crenellations for defending archers, turning the temple into a true bastion of faith.
Moat and Drawbridge
A deep moat surrounds the temple with a sturdy drawbridge, deterring all but the most determined besiegers and elevating the sanctity within.
Multi-Layered Walls
Towering double or triple curtain walls, each an obstacle to the profane, making the temple a near-impenetrable holdfast of the faith.
Fortified Tower
A great central tower rises above the temple, commanding the surrounding lands and serving as a final redoubt for the defenders of the faith.
Sanctuary Citadel
An awe-inspiring fortress-temple, blending spiritual sanctity with daunting military architecture. The faith is utterly secure behind these walls.
